adversarialFindings: RESOLVED (this dispatch): countyManifestTypes.ts:78-92 MANIFEST_RAILS was the root hardcoded rail set. Deleted. The column set is now derived by deriveRails(railCapabilities, manifestCells), preferring the API ordered railCapabilities and falling back to first-appearance order in manifestCells; it returns [] when neither is served so the panel degrades honestly rather than substituting a local list.

RESOLVED (this dispatch): CountyManifestGrid.tsx:594 rendered a hardcoded /254 denominator in every rail header. It now derives from summary.totalCounties. This was a second instrument-not-data defect in the same panel, not named in the dispatch.
RESOLVED (this dispatch): PanelRegistry.ts:71 asserted 254x13 in a comment. Comment-only (never rendered), but corrected so the next reader is not misled.

RESOLVED (this dispatch): CountyManifestGrid.test.tsx pinned the grid to the frontend own constant, so the test suite could never have caught the drift - it asserted the console against the same hardcoded list the console used. Tests now use an explicit FIXTURE_RAILS fixture mirroring the live API, plus a test that feeds a rail set the frontend does not declare (including an unknown a-brand-new-rail) and asserts the grid follows the API. This is the control that makes the class of defect self-detecting.

REMAINING, NOT FIXED (accepted, presentation-only): countyManifestTypes.ts RAIL_LABELS still names 14 rail keys for short headers and long labels. This is NOT a column-set assertion - an undeclared rail still renders, using fallbackShort() to derive a header from the key. Worst case for a future unknown rail is an ugly short label, never a missing or extra column. Judged the right seam: the alternative is server-supplied display labels, which would require an API change this dispatch is forbidden to make.

REMAINING, NOT FIXED (out of scope, different panel): apps/command-center/src/admin/control/panels/CountyLedger.tsx also reads /api/county-ledger. It builds its facet ordering dynamically (line 348) and carries no hardcoded rail/facet array, so it is not exposed to this defect class. No action needed.

REMAINING, NOT FIXED (infrastructure, pre-existing): the root .vercel/project.json is linked to property-explorer while apps/command-center/.vercel is linked to cmdcenter. A root deploy therefore lands on property-explorer by default. The reverse also bites: deploying from apps/command-center FAILS the build (ERR_PNPM_NO_MATCHING_VERSION_INSIDE_WORKSPACE - @hauska/map-renderer not found inside the workspace) because only that subtree uploads and the workspace sibling in packages/ is absent. cmdcenter must be deployed from the REPO ROOT using the root vercel.json (installCommand pnpm install --no-frozen-lockfile, buildCommand pnpm --filter ./apps/command-center build), after re-linking root to cmdcenter and restoring the link afterwards. The alternating Ready/Error pattern in vercel ls cmdcenter --prod (Errors at 42s, 3d, 4d with 2-3s durations vs Ready at 26-28s) shows prior operators hit this exact trap repeatedly. Durable fix would be a per-app deploy script or a Root Directory setting on the cmdcenter project; not attempted here as it is outside a display-fix dispatch.
